note: Japanese words are spelled the way the voice should say them (Toh-moh-shee-bee, oh-foo-dah, moh-ree shee-oh, oh-soh).

scenes.show: Cold open: a close look at a candle about to go out, its seconds ticking.
The gate. Nothing moves yet. (6 s: the voice and a breath.)
scenes.text: Toh-moh-shee-bee. The Candle Ledger. A to-do app where fear shows you what is urgent.

scenes.show: Enter the board, then cut to one card: assignee, fields, links.
scenes.text: Each task is an oh-foo-dah, a paper talisman, with a candle beside it. The candle is the time left. Cards carry assignees, project fields, and links to GitHub or Google Docs.

scenes.show: Close: an urgent card glows. A shadow passes. Close: the candle eaten shorter than its clock.
scenes.text: When a deadline is close, the card glows. Sometimes the candle looks shorter than the clock says. Something has been eating the wax. The deadline itself never changes.

scenes.show: Press the jack-o'-lantern. Submit with no title: close on the salt. Then fill in the task.
scenes.text: Press the jack-o'-lantern to add a task. Leave the title empty, and a mound of salt appears. In Japan, moh-ree shee-oh, piled salt, keeps unwanted things away. Here, it keeps out bad input.

scenes.show: Close: hold the seal to finish a task. Close: add wax to another.
scenes.text: To finish, press and hold to peel off the seal, so nothing ends by mistake. Running late? Add wax.

scenes.show: Close: the overdue seal in English, then in Japanese. The light theme, then back.
scenes.text: English and Japanese, dark and light. A few words stay Japanese in every language, like this seal. Oh-soh. Overdue.

scenes.show: The last seconds of the candle, close, with the counting song. Then the curse, trimmed.
scenes.text: And if you let a candle burn out.

scenes.show: Safe mode on (close on the switch). Then a task is finished with the seal, close: the ledger still works.
scenes.text: The curse comes only once for each task. Safe mode turns every effect off, and the ledger still works. Sign in to share it across devices, or add candles through the API. Built with Kiro, for Kiroween. Toh-moh-shee-bee. Do not let a candle die alone.
